import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 644

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/644](https://www.erdosproblems.com/644)
- [EFKT92] Erdős, P. and Fon-Der-Flaass, D. and Kostochka, A. V. and Tuza, Zs., Small transversals in
  uniform hypergraphs. Siberian Adv. Math. (1992), 82-88.
-/

namespace Erdos644

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
Let $f(k,r)$ be minimal such that if $A_1,A_2,\ldots$ is a family of sets, all of size $k$, such
that for every collection of $r$ of the $A_is$ there is some pair $\{x,y\}$ which intersects all of
the $A_j$, then there is some set of size $f(k,r)$ which intersects all of the sets $A_i$. Is it
true that
$$f(k,7)=(1+o(1))\frac{3}{4}k?$$
Is it true that for any $r\geq 3$ there exists some constant $c_r$ such that
$$f(k,r)=(1+o(1))c_rk?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_644.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔
    (fun k ↦ ((Hypergraph.subfamilyTransversalBound k 7 2).toNat : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun k ↦ (3 / 4 : ℝ) * k) := by
  sorry

/--
For every $r\geq 3$, is there $c_r>0$ such that $f(k,r)=(1+o(1))c_rk$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_644.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r : ℕ, 3 ≤ r → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
    (fun k ↦ ((Hypergraph.subfamilyTransversalBound k r 2).toNat : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun k ↦ c * k) := by
  sorry

end Erdos644

reformulations.difference: The imported extremal function imposes the two-point transversal condition on subfamilies of at most seven edges, whereas the source says collections of seven sets. These conventions can give different extremal values for small parameters, but not different answers to this asymptotic question.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let g(k,r) be the imported bound and f(k,r) the bound using exactly r-edge subfamilies. For k>0, g(k,r) ≤ f(k,r) ≤ max(g(k,r),r−1): a family with at least r edges allows every smaller subfamily to be extended to r edges, while a family with fewer than r nonempty edges has a transversal of size at most r−1. Thus, for r=7, either asserted asymptotic relation to (3/4)k forces f and g to be eventually equal. The full equivalence is proved as Review644.part_i_equiv_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorry dependencies.

reformulations.difference: Besides using subfamilies of at most r edges, Lean explicitly requires c_r>0; the source merely says that there is some constant c_r.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed r≥3, the comparison g(k,r) ≤ f(k,r) ≤ max(g(k,r),r−1) makes asymptotic equivalence to c_r k identical for every positive c_r. Positivity is redundant: for k>0 a single nonempty k-edge gives g(k,r)≥1, hence also f(k,r)≥1. Asymptotic equivalence of either eventually positive sequence to c_r k forces c_r>0. The equivalence including the quantifiers ∀ r≥3 and ∃ c_r, and the removal/addition of the positivity condition, is proved as Review644.part_ii_equiv_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorry dependencies.
